title: sets and membership algorithms
concepts: A set represents distinct values without attaching a separate value to each key
Membership queries can replace repeated scans when the data supports efficient lookup
Set operations combine or compare collections according to mathematical definitions
Hash-based sets offer expected constant-time membership under suitable hashing assumptions, while ordered sets preserve sorted order at a different cost
Deduplication changes the representation and may discard order or multiplicity
The correct equality relation and comparer are part of the problem definition

practiceProblems.name: Contains Duplicate
practiceProblems.statement: Return true if any value occurs at least twice in nums; otherwise return false.

practiceProblems.name: Intersection of Two Arrays
practiceProblems.statement: Return the unique values present in both integer arrays. Result order is unrestricted.

practiceProblems.name: Happy Number
practiceProblems.statement: Repeatedly replace a positive integer by the sum of the squares of its decimal digits. Return true if the process reaches 1 and false if it enters a cycle that excludes 1.

practiceProblems.name: Jewels and Stones
practiceProblems.statement: Count how many characters in stones are also present in jewels. Matching is case-sensitive.
constraints: Both contain English letters; characters in jewels are unique.

practiceProblems.name: Unique Number of Occurrences
practiceProblems.statement: Return true if every distinct value in arr has a different occurrence count; otherwise return false.

accuracyFacts: HashSet membership and updates are expected O(1) under suitable hashing, not strict worst-case O(1); collisions can degrade performance and growth can cause occasional O(n) resizing.
SortedSet uses comparer ordering, and values for which the comparer returns zero are treated as equivalent duplicates. Its operations are typically O(log n).
IReadOnlySet<T> restricts mutation through that interface but does not make the underlying collection immutable or protect against mutation through other references.
HashSet<T> uses EqualityComparer<T>.Default unless a comparer is supplied; mutable equality/hash state can make stored elements difficult to find. SortedSet<T> relies on its ordering comparer.
Intersection of Two Arrays requires unique output in unrestricted order, not multiset intersection; canonical examples and constraints checked against LeetCode.
Happy Number transformation is deterministic; a repeated non-1 state proves a cycle that cannot later reach 1. The stated positive 32-bit constraints and examples checked against LeetCode.
Jewels and Stones is case-sensitive and counts each stone character occurrence, including repeated characters; constraints and examples checked against LeetCode.
Unique Number of Occurrences checks that frequencies of distinct values are unique; constraints and examples checked against LeetCode.
